**Wire verb `ptmqtl pairs`**: PTM-PTM pairs within one dataset: two modifications identified together on one peptidoform (physical), and two sites whose occupancies rise and fall together across runs (co-varying), with Benjamini-Hochberg q-values.

# Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Unit | Range | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `observations` (wire `--observations`) | `path` | required | — | — | ptmqtl occupancy's observations table, with the same rules: a header row naming run, full\_sequence, protein\_accession, start\_residue, end\_residue (1-based), intensity (instrument units; blank, NA or NaN is identified but not quantified) and optionally previous\_residue; one row per (run, peptidoform, protein), MS/MS identifications only. |
| `pair_type` (wire `--type`) | `string` | required | — | `physical \| covarying \| both` | Which pairs: physical (PtmPairEngine.Physical, mzLib's type P), covarying (PtmPairEngine.CoVarying, type A), or both, physical rows first. Required: they are different evidence, and mzLib has no default between its two methods. |
| `samples` (wire `--samples`) | `path` | absent | — | — | Optional. ptmqtl occupancy's run-to-sample table (a header row, then run, sample). With it the observations are first combined per sample by mzLib's CombineObservations, so both pair types are computed across samples rather than fractions. Map only fractions together. Absent, none is sent: pairs are across runs. |
| `modifications` (wire `--modifications`) | `string` | absent | — | `exact names, tab-separated, none blank` | Optional. As ptmqtl occupancy: count only these modifications (Category:IdWithMotif, separated by tabs) as sites. Not with categories. Absent, no filter. |
| `categories` (wire `--categories`) | `string` | absent | — | `category names, tab-separated, none blank` | Optional. As ptmqtl occupancy: count only modifications of these categories. Not with modifications. Absent, no filter. |
| `min_quantified_fraction` (wire `--min-quantified-fraction`) | `float` | `mzLib's PtmPairEngine.DefaultMinQuantifiedFraction, 0.7 at the pin` | fraction of the runs (0 to 1) | `> 0 and <= 1` | Co-varying only. A site enters co-varying pairs only if its occupancy is quantified (a ceiling counts only with keep-ceiling) in at least this fraction of the runs, rounded up: the runs (or samples) where any site was identified or covered, reported as covarying\_run\_count. Absent, the bridge sends none and mzLib's default applies. |
| `keep_ceiling` (wire `--keep-ceiling`) | `flag` | `absent: mzLib's excludeCeiling default, true at the pin, so ceilings are left out` | — | — | Co-varying only. Keep a run where a site was seen only modified (a fraction of 1 with unmodified\_quantified false). Two unrelated sites both read 1 in low-load runs, so ceilings can correlate sites through detection alone; mzLib leaves them out unless asked. |
| `remove_run_level` (wire `--remove-run-level`) | `flag` | `absent: mzLib's removeRunLevel default, false at the pin` | — | — | Co-varying only. Correlate given each run's level: the partial Spearman correlation with the run's median occupancy over the other tested sites of the pair's group (the pair's own two left out). Removes a batch or loading shift that moves many sites in the same runs. Batch only: where the run level follows the design, removing it tests the correlation within conditions instead. |
| `run_level_group` (wire `--run-level-group`) | `string` | `absent: mzLib's runLevelGroup default, null, one group of every site` | — | `category \| modification` | With remove-run-level only. Whose run level applies to a site: category, one level per modification category (mzLib's ModificationSite.Category); or modification, one level per modification name. A pair within one group is correlated given that group's level, a pair across two groups given both. Not with run-level-groups. |
| `run_level_groups` (wire `--run-level-groups`) | `path` | absent | — | — | With remove-run-level only. A TSV with a header row, then modification, group: one row per modification name, mapping it to its group, for example every phosphorylation to phospho. Every modification among the sites needs a group. The wire form of mzLib's runLevelGroup for any grouping, such as chemistry. Not with run-level-group. |

Per-row fields (one value per record, in `columns` or each list entry):

| Field | Type | Unit | Null? | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `result_type` | `string` | — | never | physical (mzLib's PairResultType P: both modifications identified on one peptidoform, so on one molecule) \| covarying (type A: occupancies correlated across runs). |
| `site_a` | `string` | — | never | The first site's key, as ptmqtl occupancy's site\_key; ordinally before site\_b. A pair is written once. |
| `site_b` | `string` | — | never | The second site's key. |
| `same_protein` | `bool` | — | never | Both sites on the same protein accession. |
| `overlapping` | `bool` | — | never | Some peptide covers both sites: one span on one protein, or one peptide (by base sequence) mapped to both proteins. Always true for physical. A co-varying overlapping pair shares peptides, so it is correlated by construction, and is left out of its family's adjustment. |
| `statistic` | `float` | physical: fraction (0 to 1), co-occupancy; covarying: unitless correlation (-1 to 1) | yes: physical: never quantified together in any run; covarying: not\_estimable | physical: median over runs of the co-occupancy, the intensity of peptidoforms carrying both modifications over the intensity of peptidoforms covering both positions. covarying: Spearman's rho of the two occupancies across runs; with the run level removed, the partial rho given it. |
| `p_value` | `float` | fraction (0 to 1) | yes: physical (no test in this mzLib), or not\_estimable | Two-sided Spearman p-value against rho = 0, computed as spearman\_method says. |
| `q` | `float` | fraction (0 to 1) | yes: not tested: physical, overlapping, or not\_estimable | Benjamini-Hochberg adjusted p within fdr\_family, over that family's non-overlapping pairs. Not a target-decoy q-value. |
| `fdr_family` | `string` | — | never | The family the adjustment runs over, mzLib's PtmPair.FdrFamily verbatim: P or A (physical or co-varying), then intra (same protein) or inter, for example A:inter. |
| `n` | `int` | runs | never | physical: runs where a doubly modified peptidoform was identified. covarying: runs where both occupancies were quantified (with the run level removed, and had a level). |
| `statistic_n` | `int` | runs | never | Runs statistic was computed on. physical: runs where the doubly modified form and the forms covering both positions were quantified, at most n. covarying: equal to n. |
| `spearman_method` | `string` | — | yes: physical: no correlation | exact (the full permutation distribution, for 9 or fewer runs without ties, plain only) \| asymptotic (t on n - 2 degrees of freedom, or n - 2 - k given k run levels: one, or two for a pair across groups, less any level the other carries entirely) \| not\_estimable (too few runs, a constant occupancy, or with the run level removed fewer than min\_runs\_for\_run\_level runs). |
| `run_level_removed` | `bool` | — | never | Whether statistic and p\_value are the partial correlation given the run level. Always false for physical. |

# Caveats

- physical: both modifications on one peptidoform, so on one molecule. statistic is the median co-occupancy over the statistic\_n runs where both were quantified. There is no test in this mzLib: p\_value and q are null.
- covarying: Spearman's rho across runs on the runs where both sites are quantified. Floors and not\_detected cells are not values and are left out, and so, unless keep-ceiling, are ceilings.
- A site enters co-varying pairs only if quantified in at least min\_quantified\_fraction of covarying\_run\_count, rounded up.
- q is Benjamini-Hochberg within fdr\_family. An overlapping pair is reported with q null: shared peptides correlate it by construction. q is not a target-decoy q-value.
- With remove-run-level, a run's level is the median occupancy there of the other tested sites of the pair's group; a run with fewer than min\_sites\_for\_run\_level such sites has no level, and a pair sharing fewer than min\_runs\_for\_run\_level runs with a level is not\_estimable (the partial test's t on n - 3 df is too liberal there). Use it for a batch or loading shift only: where the run level follows the design, it removes the effect under study.
- The observations follow ptmqtl occupancy's rules and exclusions: MS/MS identifications only, one row per (run, peptidoform, protein).
